title: COWS (Clinical Opiate Withdrawal Scale)
sources: Wesson DR, Ling W. J Psychoactive Drugs 2003; ASAM / SAMHSA buprenorphine induction guidance
purpose: Objectifies opioid withdrawal severity (11 items, total 0–48). Its main use is timing buprenorphine induction — enough withdrawal must be present (typically COWS ≥ 8, many protocols ≥ 12) so that buprenorphine does not precipitate withdrawal.

items.label: Sweating (past 30 min, not from room temperature / activity)

options.label: No report of chills or flushing
Flushed or observable moistness on face
Beads of sweat on brow or face
Reports difficulty sitting still, but able to
Frequent shifting or extraneous limb movements
Unable to sit still for more than a few seconds
Pinned or normal for room light
Possibly larger than normal for room light
So dilated that only the rim of the iris is visible

items.label: Bone or joint aches (if withdrawal is the cause)

options.label: Severe diffuse aching of joints / muscles
Rubbing joints or muscles, unable to sit still from discomfort

items.label: Runny nose or tearing (not from cold / allergies)

options.label: Nasal stuffiness or unusually moist eyes
Nose constantly running or tears streaming
Patient reports increasing irritability or anxiousness
So irritable / anxious that participation is difficult
Piloerection can be felt or hairs standing up on the arms

interpretation.label: Mild withdrawal — generally too early for a first buprenorphine dose in a standard protocol (some ED protocols start at ≥ 8)
Moderate withdrawal — appropriate to begin buprenorphine induction (e.g. 4–8 mg SL, then reassess)
Moderately severe withdrawal — buprenorphine induction; higher first dose reasonable

notes: Precipitated withdrawal risk is highest with methadone or a fentanyl-heavy supply (fentanyl body stores). 'High-dose' or 'macro-dose' buprenorphine induction and low-dose (Bernese) micro-induction are alternatives when the standard approach is difficult — use a local protocol. Treat symptoms symptomatically in the meantime (clonidine, ondansetron, loperamide, an NSAID).
